description: Participants handle an analytical engagement for a fictional university's student-success unit. They test requests against the Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL), classify the data and decide what may be shared with a government partner, suppress small cells in aggregate outputs, compare outcome and error rates across student groups, keep an analysis log and a datasheet, and handle three stakeholder conversations: scoping, pushing back on an unsafe request and explaining limits. Deeper de-identification and fairness audits are in DS-309.
audience: Practitioners. Graduates and early-career analysts who have completed the FN courses or passed the placement test, and analysts moving into data science.
prerequisites: FN-106 Responsible Data and AI Practice in the Kingdom
Computes rates and a confidence interval for a proportion by group in SQL or a dataframe
Has written a short analytical report for a non-specialist reader

outcomes.text: Explain the PDPL principles and the classification and sharing rules an analysis engages, from lawful basis to data subjects' rights and transfer, given five analysis requests from the case
outcomes.evidence: a note per request naming the rules engaged, at least four of five right

outcomes.text: Classify the datasets and outputs of an analysis and decide what may be shared, with whom and in what form, given the student records, a partner's sharing request and the classification policy
outcomes.evidence: a classification and sharing table with the control each decision requires

outcomes.text: Apply aggregation and small-cell suppression to results tables and check that no student can be singled out, given draft tables by college, nationality and disability status
outcomes.evidence: release-ready tables and a log of each suppressed cell and the reason

outcomes.text: Analyse referral and error rates across student groups and report differences with their uncertainty and possible causes, given a support-referral rule and its results by group
outcomes.evidence: rates with intervals and two possible bias types with the check that separates them

outcomes.text: Prepare a datasheet and an analysis log that let a reviewer trace each result to its data, decisions and approvals, given the case analysis and a template
outcomes.evidence: a datasheet and log a peer uses to answer five audit questions

outcomes.text: Lead a stakeholder conversation that rescopes an unsafe or unclear request into a lawful, answerable question, and record the agreement, given a role-played sponsor asking for an individual-level risk list
outcomes.evidence: an observed role-play scored on a rubric and a written scope note
